Jeesal Akman Care Corporation (Directors: ) was the care provider for JCP and closed in May 2021. However, Jeesal Holdings Ltd (JHL) and Jeesal Residential Care Services Ltd (JRCSL) and possibly other linked companies with the same Directors, continue to provide residential care to persons with mental health illness, learning disabilities, complex needs and physical disability. The concerns raised at the inquest could apply to residential care offered by these companies and unless such concerns
residential care for persons with learning disabilities and mental health illness without adequate oversight



CCTV was shown at the inquest which revealed Ben King had been assaulted in the hours prior to his death and also that 1 to 1 observation was not carried out in accordance with the Observations Policy
failure to monitor residents with 1-to-1 observation


Basic dietary advice and guidance provided was not followed by staff
non-compliance with dietary guidance


The use of the Dietician in training of staff was reduced in 2017 from one day's training to an hour's power point presentation
inadequate staff training on dietary management


Important records were not completed by staff, eg Food intake, Exercise, Weight and vital observations
incomplete health monitoring records


Evidence was heard that exercise was not regularly offered to Ben King and when the Sports Instructor was absent for lengthy periods of time, there was no replacement
lack of regular exercise for residents with learning disabilities


The present Falls Policy does not comply with NICE Guidelines
non-compliant falls policy


Evidence was heard that a Falls Policy was drafted, and a Risk Assessment trialled at the beginning of 2020, the Covid-19 pandemic intervened and delayed its completion
incomplete falls policy development


There is no person appointed as Falls Lead. The job application has not yet been advertised, although it is recognised that someone is required to lead the Falls process
no falls lead appointed


Staff will need training and the training package has not yet been developed
lack of staff training


Assisted Technology is being considered to alert staff to movements and the needs of patients. This has not been progressed since October 2021 and is still at an early stage
delayed assisted technology implementation



There is no requirement for a risk assessment to be carried out before a patient is placed in a side room (other than for risk of falls), so as to identify if they will have any risks and difficulties associated with communicating their needs to staff in an emergency situation.
patient placed in side room without risk assessment



There is no formal requirement to ensure that a patient is risk assessed with regard to ability to use a call bell and, if they are unable, to consider suitable alternatives, especially when in a side room and there is no other way to attract staff attention.
patient unable to use call bell without alternatives


communication between teams, particularly to the staff on duty at night as to what information was handed over
communication errors during handover



The doctor had not read the ambulance electronic records and was not aware of a system in place to obtain these notes prior to his seeing the patient. These notes contained information about Mr Havard having hematemesis and two doses of morphine given to Mr Havard by the crew. He did examine Mr Havard and had differential diagnoses and went to speak to the locum consultant who was just coming on shift for advice. The consultant did not ask to see the notes from the crew or the hospital notes and
failure to review ambulance records before discharge


That the prescription of Beriplex was not given in a timely manner
delayed administration of reversal medication


That no-one checked that it had been given despite an extension of the bleed
lack of verification of medication administration


That no-one seemed to know why it was not given as ordered or where Mr Potts was on the day in question
unclear medication administration and patient location tracking



It became clear during evidence, that members of staff are not aware of what is required of them when they carry out Observations on a patient. This was particularly evident with regard to Observations to be carried out on a "two members of staff to one patient" basis. Areas of confusion include how staff are to engage with a patient, how close they are required to be with regard to the patient, i.e. at arm's length or within eyesight and how to record the information gained from the Observation
staff unawareness of observation requirements



The Escort Policy does not include information relating to the transfer of patients from one place to another (in this case from an Acute Hospital to the Fermoy Unit) when other services are involved, for.instance the Police. In particular, Mr Higgins who had been acting in an unpredictable and paranoid manner, was put into a cage at the rear of the Police van with three Police Officers, with no Mental Health staff to accompany him
inadequate escort policy for patient transfer



The safety of the environment where the incident took place, namely a disabled ramp with a railing along the edge and a concrete'floor, had not been risk assessed prior to taking Mr Higgins outside for a cigarette
unassessed disabled ramp safety



There is no agreement in place between the NSFT and the Acute Hospital as to the best way to deal with patients subject to detention under the Mental Health Act who require assessment and treatment at A & E, as a result of which Mr Higgins, was required to wait over 2 hours in a busy, public area, having already self-harmed and shown signs of paranoia
lack of protocol for detained patient assessment
